acceptance: An ADR-0139 amendment records the decision, with measured admitted width and past-wave conflict data for each option
With a cmd/evolve lane in flight, a Go lane in an unrelated package is admitted (red test first), if the ADR picks option a or b
No two admitted lanes edit the same package cell
fix: Write an ADR-0139 amendment that compares three options: (a) drop reach for high fan-out roots such as cmd/evolve, mirroring how hubs drop it for high fan-in; (b) use direct imports instead of transitive deps; (c) keep reach and accept the width. Measure each option on the wave 129 backlog copy (lanes admitted, and the conflict rate on past waves), then implement the winner with a pinning test.
routed_reason: changes the admission safety policy; needs an ADR-0139 decision
summary: footprintOf (go/internal/admission/admission.go:96-105) puts the transitive deps of every edited package into reach. An edit of cmd/evolve therefore reaches almost every non-hub package, and only 6 hubs exist at hub_min_importers=120. In the wave 129 reproduction, with a cmd/evolve lane in flight, admission admitted only 4 docs-only items out of 22 candidates. This limits width even after the pool gets the ranked backlog (fix/pool-plan-supplies-ranked-backlog). It changes the admission safety policy, so it needs an ADR-0139 decision first.
title: Admission by cell: an edit of cmd/evolve reaches almost every package, so a Go lane cannot run beside it
